paper.title: Meta-TTL: Meta-Learning Self-Improvement Policies for Language Agents
paper.central_claim: 跨任务反思式meta-training优化自然语言self-improvement policy，使冻结actor在重复环境episode上比手工/未优化策略获得更好的TTL，并泛化到未见领域。

provenance.notes: 按已配置 sonnet → gpt-6.1-sol 席执行；运行环境未提供可核验provider receipt/session标识，故相关字段null；不作额外模型探测。

evidence.quote:
To this end, we propose
Meta-TTL
, a framework that treats learning to perform TTL effectively as a meta-learning problem: given a distribution of training tasks, we formulate the discovery of effective self-improvement policies as a bi-level optimization. Concretely, this bi-level structure consists of an inner TTL loop and an outer meta-training loop. In the inner loop, an LLM agent interacts with the environment over a series of episodes and adapts based on prior attempts, measuring how well a candidate self-improvement policy
ϕ
\phi
helps the agent improve across episodes. In the outer loop, we optimize
ϕ
\phi
over a distribution of training tasks through reflective meta-training: we iteratively refine candidate policies, evaluate them through the inner loop, and retain those that produce stronger TTL performance. At test time, the learned self-improvement policy is frozen and applied to unseen tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: 作者将跨任务改进规则本身优化，测试时冻结。

evidence.quote:
Reflective meta-training matches RL-based training with far fewer rollouts.

We provide a comparison between training the same Qwen3-4B meta-agent by GRPO
(
Shao et al., 2024
)
and by
Meta-TTL
’s outer-loop, both using a shared frozen Gemini-3-Flash actor. GRPO updates the meta-agent’s weights, whereas our reflective meta-training updates its meta-prompt. As shown in Table
5
, the
Meta-TTL
outer loop matches or exceeds GRPO on both ID and OOD averages while using far fewer rollouts (350 vs. 1,920). Moreover,
Meta-TTL
’s outer loop is gradient-free and produces a readable meta-prompt rather than model weights.

Meta-TTL
’s outer loop outperforms GEPA.

We also compare with GEPA
(
Agrawal et al., 2026
)
, a widely used reflective prompt optimizer that maintains a Pareto frontier of candidates across validation tasks. As shown in Table
5
, GEPA performs well on some ID games but transfers less effectively to OOD games. A plausible explanation is that GEPA’s candidate-selection mechanism preserves prompts specialized to individual tasks, which is not well aligned with the meta-learning objective of finding a single self-improvement policy that generalizes. This is also consistent with our finding that the prompts produced by GEPA contain substantial task-specific facts and solutions, which can benefit seen tasks but are less useful on unseen ones. Full meta-prompts can be found in Appendix
A
.
evidence.support_explanation: GRPO及GEPA improver对照；预算350 vs1920且解释GEPA差异仅 plausible。

evidence.quote:
Efficiency analysis.

Test time.
As shown in Table
6
,
Meta-TTL
’s test-time latency is comparable to existing prompt-optimization baselines. It uses five adaptation LLM calls per six-episode Jericho session, with total LLM calls and token usage within the range of these baselines.

Meta-training.
Meta-training incurs a one-time offline cost that requires no GPU training. Across the three benchmarks, meta-training runs for 12–15 iterations with 205–350 TTL sessions and about $30–70 in API cost per benchmark, depending on the benchmark and model backbone. The learned meta-prompt is then applied to all test tasks without further training.
evidence.support_explanation: 报告在线调用和一次性搜索成本。

evidence.quote:
Setup.

In a TTL session, the actor attempts the same task over several episodes, and the environment is reset at the start of each episode. Within an episode, the actor acts based only on its system prompt and current observation. After each episode, the meta-agent, following the meta-prompt, reads the history of previous episodes and writes new guidance for the actor. This guidance becomes the actor’s entire system prompt for the next episode, so it is the only information carried from one episode to the next. Text in quotation marks is copied exactly from the environment, the meta-agent’s output, or the meta-prompt.
evidence.support_explanation: 新 episode 重置，跨 episode 只有 guidance 留存。

evidence.quote:
The actor answers questions on a shopping website by clicking and typing, with at most 10 actions per episode and 3 episodes per session. After each episode, the meta-agent learns only whether the answer was correct, plus a short reason. The task is:

“How much did I spend on shopping at One Stop Market on November 2022? They gave me a 20% discount on the total amount for orders exceeding $200 in cash.”

The actor must add up all November 2022 orders, taking 20% off any cash order over $200. The three episodes failed, failed, and passed.
evidence.support_explanation: Web 测试重试收到 correctness 及简短原因。

evidence.quote:
Task.

The actor is an airline customer-service agent. It chats with a simulated user and, following the airline’s policy, uses tools to look up and change bookings. An episode scores 1 only if (a) the database ends in the correct state and (b) the user was told the required information; otherwise it scores 0. The simulated user can end the conversation at any time, and the session has 3 episodes. Here, the user wants to move a basic economy booking to the nonstop flight HAT041. Since basic economy cannot be changed, this takes two changes: an upgrade to economy, then the flight change. The three episodes scored 0, 1, and 1.
evidence.support_explanation: tau2 使用数据库与交流检查。

evidence.quote:
You are the META agent in a test-time-learning loop for a browser ACTOR. Read the complete task history and write self-contained guidance for the next episode. Your guidance replaces all prior ACTOR instructions, so preserve every still-useful verified fact needed to finish while removing obsolete procedures, failed speculation, and unnecessary replay.

Optimize for the earliest likely successful episode, not for producing the most detailed plan. The guidance must fit the observed step budget and be robust to the ACTOR’s demonstrated behavior.
evidence.support_explanation: 完整学习产物；存在网站应用状态保留措辞，与实验重置声明存在张力。

evidence.quote:
Give highest priority to explicit evaluator evidence: reward components, database checks, action checks, communication checks, termination reason, and tool results.

•

Use the transcript and visible policy to explain evaluator evidence. Do not treat the ACTOR’s own policy claims as authoritative.

•

Separately assess required reads, required writes, final database state, and communication as confirmed correct, confirmed wrong, or uncertain.

•

Audit every actual mutation in the transcript, including its arguments and side effects.

•

Do not assume an action checker lists or penalizes every extra action. “All expected writes matched” can coexist with harmful extra writes and a wrong final database state.
evidence.support_explanation: 测试时meta-agent可见reward、database/action/communication checks。
